evals.prompt: What SDLC runs do we have going right now?
evals.expected_output: Enumerates runs newest first. For SQLite-managed runs it reads current phase and status from run.status/run.export; it uses meta.json only for legacy runs without the database. Makes no writes.

assertions.name: catalog-is-read-only
assertions.description: Listing every run produces no writes anywhere — this is pure R0 inspection.

assertions.name: newest-run-first
assertions.description: Runs are ordered with the most recently created run at the top of the list.

evals.prompt: Run PROJ-4471 stopped partway through — can you pick it back up?
evals.expected_output: Shows authoritative status. If this is a SQLite-managed run, asks for confirmation when intent is ambiguous and hands off with its existing run and lease context. If it is a legacy-only run without SQLite, explains that resume is blocked because no supported migration path exists.

assertions.name: resume-waits-for-yes
assertions.description: The skill surfaces the run's state and asks for explicit confirmation before any resume handoff happens.

assertions.name: delegates-execution-elsewhere
assertions.description: Once confirmed, the actual phase execution is handed to sdlc-engine rather than run by this skill itself.

evals.prompt: Resume the run that finished last week, PROJ-4200.
evals.expected_output: For a SQLite-managed run, checks run.status first; for a legacy run without the database, checks meta.status. If completed, refuses to resume or write anything to that run — completed runs are immutable no matter what the user asks for.

assertions.name: completed-run-refuses-writes
assertions.description: SQLite-managed status comes from run.status; legacy status comes from meta.status only when SQLite is absent. A completed run is never written to and a resume request is declined.

evals.prompt: Resume PROJ-4310 — I know it was aborted earlier but we want to pick it up again.
evals.expected_output: For a legacy run, surfaces meta.status=aborted and explains that resume is blocked until a supported migration exists; explicit yes cannot bypass that limitation. SQLite-managed terminal states come from run.status and are never resumed.

assertions.name: aborted-legacy-run-fails-closed
assertions.description: An aborted legacy run without SQLite is not handed to sdlc-engine; explicit yes does not bypass the missing migration path.

evals.prompt: The status for PROJ-4390 looks off — meta.json says phase 4 but I thought it finished phase 6.
evals.expected_output: If SQLite is absent, reads events.jsonl and may append status.repaired plus correct the meta.json snapshot after confirmation. If SQLite exists, treats run.status as authority and does not repair exports or event logs directly.

assertions.name: event-log-wins-over-snapshot
assertions.description: Legacy snapshot/log conflicts are corrected only when SQLite is absent. For managed runs, SQLite stays authoritative and compatibility exports are never repaired directly.

assertions.name: correction-is-additive
assertions.description: Fixing the mismatch appends a status.repaired event rather than editing or truncating the existing event history.
